id: title:ablaszkiewicz:only ship suppression rules the sdk can evaluate

review.posthog_relevance: Adds backend support for client-side evaluation of HogQL filters, allowing unsupported operators to be excluded from client-side processing and evaluated server-side instead.
review.reason: The chunk P1.F1.H2 adds the CLIENT_EVALUABLE_OPERATORS set and the backend check to exclude unsupported operators, while P1.F3.H1 adds the corresponding frontend check. This demonstrates a substantive, bounded capability improvement: the backend and frontend are both updated to support the client-side evaluation workflow, excluding unsupported operators. This is not a narrow change
review.uncertainty: The chunk does not include the actual client-side evaluation implementation, so the benefit is not fully demonstrated. The tier is assigned based on the backend and frontend support, not the client-side implementation.

observations.limitations: This chunk does not include the backend implementation of the client-side evaluation, only the backend filtering and frontend display. The backend P1.F1.H2 adds the CLIENT_EVALUABLE_OPERATORS check, but P1.F3.H1 only updates the frontend to display the correct evaluation mode. Without seeing the actual client-side evaluation implementation, it is not possible to assess the benefit.

observations.behavior: Adds CLIENT_EVALUABLE_OPERATORS set and checks it against the operator field in filters.
observations.posthog_connection: Checks if an operator is supported by the SDK before including the rule in client-side evaluation; unsupported operators cause the rule to be excluded and evaluated server-side.
